providers.description: Airtable records: read, create, update and delete a record in a base's table

credentials.name: airtable.access_token
credentials.description: Airtable access token sent as a bearer — a personal access token or an OAuth-issued one

operations.description: Read one record from a table — its cell values are under `fields` in the response, keyed by column name. Returns every column the token can see, in Airtable's default JSON cell format: narrowing or reformatting them needs the `fields[]` and `cellFormat` query parameters this connector cannot encode

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The base's id, the `app…` segment in the base's URL in Airtable

parameters.name: table_id
parameters.description: The table's id, the `tbl…` segment in the table's URL in Airtable. Airtable also routes this segment on a table *name*, which this connector does not accept: a name is interpolated into the URL unencoded, so one containing a space or a `/` would address the wrong route

parameters.name: record_id
parameters.description: The record's id, `rec…`. It is what a create returns and what the record's own URL ends with

fields.description: The record's cell values, keyed by column name. Individual columns are not enumerated: they are the base's own schema, which differs per base and changes at runtime — recording the envelope is what a consumer cannot infer

id.description: The record's id

operations.flux:
op airtable-record-get(base_id: String, table_id: String, record_id: String) -> Any
  description "Read one record from a table — its cell values are under `fields` in the response, keyed by column name. Returns every column the token can see, in Airtable's default JSON cell format: narrowing or reformatting them needs the `fields[]` and `cellFormat` query parameters this connector cannot encode. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/error/message`, its error code at `/error/type` in the response body."
  risk "low"
  idempotency "idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://api.airtable.com"
  url = fmt("{base}/v0/{base_id}/{table_id}/{record_id}")
  response = http.request(method: "GET", url)
  return response

operations.description: Create one record in a table. Cell values are supplied under `fields`, keyed by column name, and must already be in the exact JSON form each column expects — Airtable's `typecast` coercion cannot be requested yet (see the connector's notes). The created record, with its `rec…` id, is in the response

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The base's id, the `app…` segment in the base's URL in Airtable

parameters.name: table_id
parameters.description: The table's id, the `tbl…` segment in the table's URL in Airtable. The name form is not accepted — see `airtable-record-get`

parameters.name: cell_values
parameters.description: The record's cell values, as an object keyed by the table's column names — `{"Name": "Acme", "Status": "Open"}`. Each value must match its column's type: a single-select takes one of its configured option names, a linked-record column takes an array of `rec…` ids, a date takes an ISO 8601 string. An unknown column name is rejected, not ignored

schema.description: A map from column name to cell value. Untyped here because the columns are the base's own schema

cell_values.description: A map from column name to cell value. Untyped here because the columns are the base's own schema

fields.description: The created record's cell values as Airtable stored them, keyed by column name. Computed and formula columns appear here having been evaluated

id.description: The created record's id — what later calls address it by

operations.flux:
op airtable-record-create(base_id: String, table_id: String, cell_values: Any) -> Any
  description "Create one record in a table. Cell values are supplied under `fields`, keyed by column name, and must already be in the exact JSON form each column expects — Airtable's `typecast` coercion cannot be requested yet (see the connector's notes). The created record, with its `rec…` id, is in the response. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/error/message`, its error code at `/error/type` in the response body."
  risk "medium"
  idempotency "non_idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://api.airtable.com"
  url = fmt("{base}/v0/{base_id}/{table_id}")
  content_type = "application/json"
  payload = { fields: cell_values }
  response = http.request(body: payload, headers: { "content-type": content_type }, method: "POST", url)
  return response

operations.description: Update one record's cell values. The write is sparse: only the columns named in `fields` change and every other column of the record is left exactly as it was. Values must already be in the form each column expects — `typecast` coercion cannot be requested yet. The updated record is in the response

parameters.name: record_id

parameters.name: cell_values
parameters.description: The columns to change, as an object keyed by the table's column names. Columns not named here keep their current values. Setting a column to `null` clears it, which is the only way to empty a cell through this operation

cell_values.description: A map from column name to cell value. Untyped here because the columns are the base's own schema

createdTime.description: When the record was created — unchanged by an update

fields.description: The record's cell values after the update, keyed by column name. Every column is returned, not only the changed ones

id.description: The record's id

credentials.description: An Algolia API key with the ACLs this connector needs: `search` and `browse` for the reads, `addObject` and `deleteObject` for the writes. Scope it to the indices this connection should reach rather than using the Admin key

operations.description: List the indices in this Algolia application, with each index's record count and size. This is the call that discovers the index names every other operation here takes

dataSize.description: The size of the index's records in bytes

entries.description: How many records the index holds

fileSize.description: The size of the index on disk in bytes, records plus internal structures

lastBuildTimeS.description: How long the index's last build took, in seconds

name.description: The index name — what every other operation here passes as `index_name`

numberOfPendingTasks.description: Indexing operations accepted but not yet applied. Non-zero means a recent write is not visible to search yet

pendingTask.description: Whether any indexing operation is still pending

primary.description: For a replica index, the name of the index it replicates. Absent on a primary

operations.description: Search one index and return the matching records. Algolia ranks results by its own configured relevance, so the order is the index's, not this connector's; `hits_per_page` and `page` walk the result set, and `filters` narrows it with Algolia's filter syntax over the index's own attributes

parameters.name: index_name
parameters.description: The index to search, from algolia-index-list's `name` field

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The search text. An empty string matches every record in the index, ranked by the index's own ranking rules — which is how this operation browses rather than searches

parameters.name: hits_per_page
parameters.description: How many records to return per page. Algolia's own default is 20 and its maximum is 1000

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Which page of results to return, counting from 0

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: An Algolia filter expression over this index's own attributes, e.g. `category:book AND price < 20`. The attribute names are the index's content and are not knowable here; an index that has not declared an attribute as filterable answers a filter on it with a 400

exhaustiveNbHits.description: False when `nbHits` is an approximation, which Algolia does for very large result sets

hits.description: The matching records, in Algolia's ranked order. Each hit is the stored record itself — its attributes are this index's own content and are not knowable at build time — plus `objectID` and Algolia's `_highlightResult` annotations

objectID.description: The record's own id — what algolia-object-get, -save and -delete address it by

nbHits.description: How many records matched in total, which may exceed what this page returned

nbPages.description: How many pages the result set has at this `hitsPerPage`

page.description: The page that was returned, counting from 0

params.description: Echoes the search parameters Algolia actually applied, URL-encoded

processingTimeMS.description: How long Algolia spent on the query, in milliseconds

operations.flux:
op algolia-index-search(index_name: String, query: String, hits_per_page: Number, page: Number, filters: String) -> Any
  description "Search one index and return the matching records. Algolia ranks results by its own configured relevance, so the order is the index's, not this connector's; `hits_per_page` and `page` walk the result set, and `filters` narrows it with Algolia's filter syntax over the index's own attributes. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message` in the response body."
  risk "low"
  idempotency "idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://{app_id}.algolia.net"
  X_Algolia_Application_Id = "{app_id}"
  url = fmt("{base}/1/indexes/{index_name}")
  response = http.request(headers: { "X-Algolia-Application-Id": X_Algolia_Application_Id }, method: "GET", query: { filters, hitsPerPage: hits_per_page, page, query }, url)
  return response

operations.description: Save one record at a known object id, creating it if it does not exist and REPLACING it wholesale if it does. This is not a partial update: attributes absent from the body are removed from the stored record. Algolia applies the write asynchronously, so the response's `taskID` is an acknowledgement of acceptance rather than of visibility, and a search run immediately afterwards may still return the old record
operations.repeatable_because: the body carries the record's whole content as an absolute value rather than a delta, so re-sending it leaves the record in the state the caller asked for, however many times it runs. Conditional rather than idempotent because Algolia applies the write asynchronously and answers each call with a fresh `taskID`, so a stored result must never be served in place of running it

parameters.name: index_name
parameters.description: The index to write to, from algolia-index-list's `name` field. Algolia creates an index that does not exist on first write

parameters.name: object_id
parameters.description: The id to store the record under. An existing record at this id is replaced in full

body.description: The record to store, as a flat or nested JSON object. Its attributes are this index's own content model and are not knowable at build time — see the header comment for why this is one opaque schema rather than named fields. An `objectID` inside the body is redundant with the one in the path and Algolia takes the path's

body_schema.description: The record to store, as a flat or nested JSON object. Its attributes are this index's own content model and are not knowable at build time — see the header comment for why this is one opaque schema rather than named fields. An `objectID` inside the body is redundant with the one in the path and Algolia takes the path's

objectID.description: The id the record was stored under, echoed back

taskID.description: Algolia's own id for the asynchronous indexing task. The write is accepted when this returns and visible to search some time after; this connector declares no operation that waits on it

operations.flux:
op algolia-object-save(index_name: String, object_id: String, body: Any) -> Any
  description "Save one record at a known object id, creating it if it does not exist and REPLACING it wholesale if it does. This is not a partial update: attributes absent from the body are removed from the stored record. Algolia applies the write asynchronously, so the response's `taskID` is an acknowledgement of acceptance rather than of visibility, and a search run immediately afterwards may still return the old record. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message` in the response body."
  risk "high"
  idempotency "conditional"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://{app_id}.algolia.net"
  X_Algolia_Application_Id = "{app_id}"
  url = fmt("{base}/1/indexes/{index_name}/{object_id}")
  content_type = "application/json"
  payload = parse(body, as: "json")
  response = http.request(body: payload, headers: { "X-Algolia-Application-Id": X_Algolia_Application_Id, "content-type": content_type }, method: "PUT", url)
  return response

  description "Unpause a live recording."
  risk "destructive"
  idempotency "non_idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose false

  base = "https://{host}:8089/ari"
  url = fmt("{base}/recordings/live/{recordingName}/pause")
  response = http.request(method: "DELETE", url)
  return response

  description "List and filter agents. Doubles as the verification operation — cheap, read-only, and it fails loudly on a bad credential; this API has no /me endpoint"
  risk "low"
  idempotency "idempotent"
  effects ["network"]

operations.description: List the repositories in this connection's workspace, with each one's slug, name, description, main branch and privacy. Takes no argument at all: the workspace is pinned when the connection is made, so this reads exactly the workspace the operator chose and no other. Returns Bitbucket's first page only; this connector declares no page or filter parameters, and the response's `next` field carries the URL of the following page. The `slug` returned here is what every other operation in this connector takes as `repo_slug`. Also this connector's `verify`: a bounded read that runs unattended and needs nothing beyond the token and the pinned workspace

full_name.description: `workspace/slug`. Note that this is two segments: `repo_slug` is the second one alone

language.description: The primary language Bitbucket detected, empty when it detected none

links.description: Bitbucket's hypermedia links for this repository, including `html.href` — the page to give a human

project.description: The Bitbucket project grouping this repository. Left untyped rather than enumerated

size.description: The repository's size in bytes

operations.description:
Publish a new page in a space. The page is created live and visible to everyone who can see the space, is indexed for search, and notifies the space's watchers. It is created at the top level of the space unless the space's own structure places it otherwise, with no labels and no restrictions. Returns the new page's id, title and links. The content is sent as Confluence storage format — XHTML-like markup, e.g. `

text

` — not Markdown and not wiki markup

parameters.name: space_id
parameters.description: Id of the space to publish into, from `confluence-space-list`. The only field Confluence's schema strictly requires

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Constant `current` — not caller-supplied. This operation publishes a live page; a draft would be invisible and no operation here could publish it afterwards

parameters.name: title

parameters.name: body_representation
parameters.description: Constant `storage` — not caller-supplied. It fixes how Confluence interprets the content sent below

parameters.name: body

The page content, in **Confluence storage format**: XHTML-like markup such as `

A paragraph.

A heading

  • An item
`. Plain text is accepted and renders as a single unformatted run. Markdown is **not** converted — it would be stored and displayed literally, asterisks and all

body.description: Echoes the storage-format content that was sent, under `storage`. This is the one response in this connector that carries a page body — because it is the body the caller supplied, not one Confluence was asked to render

id.description: The new page's id — the only handle on it, and what `confluence-comment-add` and `confluence-page-get` address it by afterwards

parentId.description: The page it was placed under, which Confluence resolves to the space's home page when none was requested

spaceId.description: The space the page was published into

status.description: `current` on a page this operation created

title.description: Echoes the title that was sent

version.description: `{number, createdAt, authorId, minorEdit, message}`, with `number` = 1 on a page just created

providers.description: Discord bot API v10: read the bot's own identity, list the guilds it has joined, read one guild and its channels, read a channel's recent messages, and post a message. Every request authenticates as a bot — `Authorization: Bot <token>`, never `Bearer`, which is Discord's scheme word for a different credential with different reach. Every Discord id is a snowflake and is carried as a string, because a 64-bit id does not survive a JSON number. Discord rate-limits per route and answers 429 with a `Retry-After` header instead of queueing: honour it rather than retrying immediately

credentials.description: Discord bot token, sent as `Authorization: Bot <token>`. The `Bot ` scheme word is supplied by the connector; the token is the value alone. `Bearer ` is a valid Discord scheme word for a different credential — an OAuth2 user token — so sending this token with that prefix yields a 401 indistinguishable from a revoked token

operations.description: Read the bot user this token authenticates as — its snowflake id, username and application flags. Takes no argument. Also this connector's `verify`: the cheapest call that proves the token, the `Bot ` scheme word and the base URL are all correct together, and the one to run first when any other operation returns 401

operations.description: List the company's conversations in reverse chronological order (most recently updated first), first page only — this connector cannot follow Front's next-page link (see providers/front.toml's header comment). Front's structured search filter (`q`) is not accepted here: it is a bracket-notation object this pipeline cannot encode as a query string

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max conversations to return in this one page, up to Front's own cap of 100. Does not change how many pages exist, only how large this one is

_pagination.description: Carries `next`, a full absolute URL to the following page when more conversations exist. This connector cannot follow it — Front's cursor is an opaque, server-issued token unconstructable by a caller, and unencodable here regardless (C-30) — so a non-null `next` means more conversations exist beyond this first page only

next.description: Unusable here; see this field's own description

_results.description: This page's conversations, each `{id, subject, status, assignee, recipient, tags, created_at, ...}`

created_at.description: Unix timestamp, seconds

id.description: The conversation's id, prefixed `cnv_`

status.description: Front's own conversation status, e.g. `assigned`, `unassigned`, `archived` or `deleted`

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The mailbox to read: the literal `me` for the token's own mailbox, or the user's email address. `me` is what a flow should use — an address here must be one the token is authorized for, and domain-wide delegation is the only way that happens

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The message's id, the hex string Gmail's own listings and its `X-GM-MSGID` header report. It is not the RFC 2822 `Message-ID`

id.description: The message's id — what this operation takes

internalDate.description: When Gmail received it, as **epoch milliseconds in a string** — not an ISO timestamp, and not seconds. The RFC 2822 `Date` header inside `payload` may differ from it

labelIds.description: The labels applied, as ids: `INBOX`, `UNREAD`, `SENT`, `IMPORTANT`, `CATEGORY_PERSONAL`, plus any user label's opaque id. `UNREAD`'s presence is how read-state is expressed — there is no `read` boolean

payload.description: THE MESSAGE ITSELF, as a MIME tree: `{partId, mimeType, filename, headers, body, parts}`. `headers` is an **array** of `{name, value}` — so `Subject` and `From` are found by searching it, not by keying into it — and each `body.data` is **base64url-encoded**. A multipart message's text is in `parts`, not in the top-level `body`

snippet.description: A short plain-text extract of the body — the only text in this response that needs no decoding, and it is truncated

threadId.description: The conversation it belongs to. Several messages share one

operations.description: Post an event about a customer — a purchase, a page view, anything the account measures. THIS CAN CAUSE A MESSAGE TO BE SENT: an event triggers any Klaviyo flow built on its metric, so an email or SMS may reach the named profile immediately. Klaviyo creates the metric and the profile on first use if they do not exist. Answers 202 Accepted with no body: the event is queued, not confirmed. operations.description: Turn a feature flag on or off in one environment. This is a live production change: every SDK instance currently evaluating this flag in this environment — web, mobile and backend alike — switches to the other branch as soon as this call returns, for every real user it serves. It is reversible by toggling back, but it is not a private or staged edit
operations.repeatable_because: the body schema admits exactly one JSON Patch `replace` onto one environment's `on` bit (maxItems 1, op pinned to `replace`, path pinned to `/environments/{key}/on`), so it sets an absolute value and never a toggle or a delta — re-sending it lands the flag where the caller asked, however many times it runs

operations.description: Add a contact to an audience, or update the one already there. Creating with `status_if_new = "pending"` makes Mailchimp send its own opt-in confirmation and record the consent; creating with "subscribed" asserts that the account already holds that consent and sends nothing. Setting `status` on an existing contact changes whether they receive mail. This writes personal data about a third party and is not undone by calling it again

parameters.name: list_id
parameters.description: The audience id, from mailchimp-audience-list's `id`

parameters.name: subscriber_hash
parameters.description: The MD5 hash of the contact's email address, lowercased first. It is NOT the email address. Compute it caller-side from the same address passed as `email_address`, or read it from mailchimp-audience-member-list, where it is each contact's `id`. A hash that does not match `email_address` addresses a different contact

parameters.name: email_address
parameters.description: The contact's email address. Must be the address `subscriber_hash` was computed from — Mailchimp addresses the record by the hash and takes this as the address to store

parameters.name: status_if_new
parameters.description: The status to give a contact this call creates; ignored when the contact already exists. "pending" makes Mailchimp send its own opt-in confirmation email and record the consent, and is the correct value unless the account already holds documented consent for this address; "subscribed" asserts that it does and sends nothing

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The status to set on a contact that already exists. "unsubscribed" stops mail to them; "subscribed" resumes it and carries the same consent obligation as creating one. "cleaned" is Mailchimp's own marker for an address it gave up on and is not a value to set by hand

credentials.description: Okta API token, sent as `Authorization: SSWS <token>`. The `SSWS ` scheme word is supplied by the connector; the token is the value alone

operations.description: List users in the Okta org. Returns a JSON array of user objects, most recently created first. Without a filter this is the org's active user population, so use `limit` to bound it — see okta-user-get to read one user by id or login

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of users to return in this page. Okta caps this per endpoint and the cap is not declared here, so a value above it is reduced by Okta rather than rejected

response_schema.description: The org's users

created.description: When the user was created, ISO 8601

credentials.description: Which authentication providers and recovery factors are configured for this user. Never carries a password or a secret value

id.description: The user's Okta id, e.g. `00u1a2b3c4D5e6F7g8h9` — pass this as `user_id` to the other operations below

lastLogin.description: When the user last authenticated; absent for a user who never has

profile.description: The user's profile attributes. `login` and `email` are always present; an org may add custom attributes to its user schema, so this object is not exhaustively enumerated here

login.description: The user's unique sign-in identifier, usually their email address. Accepted in place of the id by okta-user-get

status.description: The user's lifecycle state. Okta's values include STAGED, PROVISIONED, ACTIVE, RECOVERY, PASSWORD_EXPIRED, LOCKED_OUT, SUSPENDED and DEPROVISIONED; treat this as an open string rather than a closed set, because Okta has added states over time

type.description: The user type this user was created with, as `{id, …}`

operations.flux:
op okta-user-list(limit: Number) -> Any
  description "List users in the Okta org. Returns a JSON array of user objects, most recently created first. Without a filter this is the org's active user population, so use `limit` to bound it — see okta-user-get to read one user by id or login"
  risk "low"
  idempotency "idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://{domain}/api/v1"
  url = fmt("{base}/users")
  response = http.request(method: "GET", query: { limit }, url)
  return response

operations.description: Deactivate a user, moving them to DEPROVISIONED. This takes effect immediately: Okta ends the person's active sessions, revokes their tokens and grants, and removes their access to every application the org assigns through Okta. They cannot sign in afterwards. An administrator can reactivate the account later, but that is a separate operation this connector does not offer, and it does not restore the sessions or tokens this call destroyed

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The user's Okta id (from okta-user-list's `id`) or their login, e.g. `ada@example.com`. Okta resolves either — confirm with okta-user-get before calling this

parameters.name: send_email
parameters.description: Set true to have Okta send its deactivation notification email. Omit for Okta's default, which sends none

operations.flux:
op okta-user-deactivate(user_id: String, send_email: Bool) -> Any
  description "Deactivate a user, moving them to DEPROVISIONED. This takes effect immediately: Okta ends the person's active sessions, revokes their tokens and grants, and removes their access to every application the org assigns through Okta. They cannot sign in afterwards. An administrator can reactivate the account later, but that is a separate operation this connector does not offer, and it does not restore the sessions or tokens this call destroyed"
  risk "destructive"
  idempotency "non_idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://{domain}/api/v1"
  url = fmt("{base}/users/{user_id}/lifecycle/deactivate")
  response = http.request(method: "POST", query: { sendEmail: send_email }, url)
  return response

config.name: domain
config.label: Okta domain
config.help: The full host you sign in to, without `https://` — if your Okta URL is `https://acme.okta.com`, this is `acme.okta.com`. European and preview orgs use `.okta-emea.com` and `.oktapreview.com`, and an org with a customised domain uses that instead, so give the whole host rather than just the first part

config.name: api_token
config.label: API token
config.help: Create one under Security → API → Tokens in the Okta Admin Console. The token inherits the permissions of the administrator who creates it, so create it as an account with only the access this connection needs — reading users and groups needs a read-only administrator, and okta-user-deactivate needs one that can manage users. Okta shows the token once, and it expires after 30 days without use

operations.description: Create a chat completion. Billed per input and output token, so the caller must state a token budget via max_completion_tokens

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to run, e.g. `gpt-4o`

parameters.name: messages
parameters.description: The conversation so far: a list of `{role, content}` objects, where role is one of system, developer, user, assistant or tool

parameters.name: max_completion_tokens
parameters.description: Upper bound on generated tokens, including reasoning tokens. Required by this connector so that every call states its cost bound

choices.description: One entry per completion; this connector never sets `n`, so there is exactly one

finish_reason.description: Why generation stopped: `stop` (the model finished), `length` (the token budget ran out and `content` is truncated), `tool_calls`, `content_filter` or `function_call`

message.description: The assistant's turn: `role`, and `content` — which is null when the model answered with `tool_calls` or set `refusal` instead

id.description: The completion's id, `chatcmpl-…`

model.description: The model that actually ran, which may name a dated snapshot of the alias that was requested

usage.description: What the call cost, in tokens: `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`, plus `completion_tokens_details` (which is where reasoning tokens are reported)

operations.flux:
op openai-chat-completion(model: String, messages: List<Any>, max_completion_tokens: Number) -> Any
  description "Create a chat completion. Billed per input and output token, so the caller must state a token budget via max_completion_tokens"
  risk "medium"
  idempotency "non_idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://api.openai.com"
  url = fmt("{base}/v1/chat/completions")
  content_type = "application/json"
  payload = { max_completion_tokens, messages, model }
  response = http.request(body: payload, headers: { "content-type": content_type }, method: "POST", url)
  return response

operations.description: Create embedding vectors for one or more input texts. Billed per input token

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The embedding model to use, e.g. `text-embedding-3-small`

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: The text to embed: a string, or an array of strings to embed as a batch

operations.description: Retrieve one stored model response by id

parameters.name: response_id
parameters.description: The ID of the response to retrieve.

anyOf.description:
Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be
useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured
format, and querying for objects via API or the dashboard.

Keys are strings with a maximum length of 64 characters. Values are strings
with a maximum length of 512 characters.
Used by OpenAI to cache responses for similar requests to optimize your cache hit rates. Replaces the `user` field. [Learn more](/docs/guides/prompt-caching).

Deprecated. Use `prompt_cache_options.ttl` instead.

The retention policy for the prompt cache. Set to `24h` to enable extended prompt caching, which keeps cached prefixes active for longer, up to a maximum of 24 hours. [Learn more](/docs/guides/prompt-caching#prompt-cache-retention).
This field expresses a maximum retention policy, while
`prompt_cache_options.ttl` expresses a minimum cache lifetime. The two
fields are independent and do not interact.
For `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.5-pro`, and future models, only `24h` is supported.

For older models that support both `in_memory` and `24h`, the default depends on your organization's data retention policy:
  - Organizations without ZDR enabled default to `24h`.
  - Organizations with ZDR enabled default to `in_memory` when `prompt_cache_retention` is not specified.

A stable identifier used to help detect users of your application that may be violating OpenAI's usage policies.
The IDs should be a string that uniquely identifies each user, with a maximum length of 64 characters. We recommend hashing their username or email address, in order to avoid sending us any identifying information. [Learn more](/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#safety-identifiers).

Specifies the processing type used for serving the request.
  - If set to 'auto', then the request will be processed with the service tier configured in the Project settings. Unless otherwise configured, the Project will use 'default'.
  - If set to 'default', then the request will be processed with the standard pricing and performance for the selected model.
  - If set to '[flex](/docs/guides/flex-processing)', then the request will be processed with the Flex Processing service tier.
  - To opt-in to [Fast mode](/api/docs/guides/fast-mode) at the request level, include the `service_tier=fast` or `service_tier=priority` parameter for Responses or Chat Completions. The response will show `service_tier=priority` regardless of if you specify `service_tier=fast` or `priority` in your request.
  - When not set, the default behavior is 'auto'.

  When the `service_tier` parameter is set, the response body will include the `service_tier` value based on the processing mode actually used to serve the request. This response value may be different from the value set in the parameter.

What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both.

An integer between 0 and 20 specifying the maximum number of most likely
tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log
probability. In some cases, the number of returned tokens may be fewer than
requested.

An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling,
where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability
mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass
are considered.

We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.

user.description:
This field is being replaced by `safety_identifier` and `prompt_cache_key`. Use `prompt_cache_key` instead to maintain caching optimizations.
A stable identifier for your end-users.
Used to boost cache hit rates by better bucketing similar requests and  to help OpenAI detect and prevent abuse. [Learn more](/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#safety-identifiers).

anyOf.description:
Whether to run the model response in the background.
[Learn more](/docs/guides/background).

The maximum number of total calls to built-in tools that can be processed in a response. This maximum number applies across all built-in tool calls, not per individual tool. Any further attempts to call a tool by the model will be ignored.

model.description:
Model ID used to generate the response, like `gpt-4o` or `o3`. OpenAI
offers a wide range of models with different capabilities, performance
characteristics, and price points. Refer to the [model guide](/docs/models)
to browse and compare available models.

anyOf.description:
The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to
create multi-turn conversations. Learn more about
[conversation state](/docs/guides/conversation-state). Cannot be used in conjunction with `conversation`.

Reference to a prompt template and its variables.
[Learn more](/docs/guides/text?api-mode=responses#reusable-prompts).

oneOf.description: A text input to the model.

prompt_cache_breakpoint.title: Prompt cache breakpoint

text.description: The text input to the model.

anyOf.title: Prompt Variables

text.description:
Configuration options for a text response from the model. Can be plain
text or structured JSON data. Learn more:
- [Text inputs and outputs](/docs/guides/text)
- [Structured Outputs](/docs/guides/structured-outputs)

format.description:
An object specifying the format that the model must output.

Configuring `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables Structured Outputs, 
which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the 
[Structured Outputs guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

The default format is `{ "type": "text" }` with no additional options.

**Not recommended for gpt-4o and newer models:**

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables the older JSON mode, which
ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON. Using `json_schema`
is preferred for models that support it.

oneOf.description: Default response format. Used to generate text responses.

type.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `text`.

oneOf.title: Text

oneOf.description:
JSON Schema response format. Used to generate structured JSON responses.
Learn more about [Structured Outputs](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

description.description:
A description of what the response format is for, used by the model to
determine how to respond in the format.

name.description:
The name of the response format. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain
underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

schema.description:
The schema for the response format, described as a JSON Schema object.
Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).
schema.title: JSON schema

anyOf.description:
Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the output.
If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined
in the `schema` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when
`strict` is `true`. To learn more, read the [Structured Outputs
guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

type.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_schema`.

oneOf.title: JSON schema

oneOf.description:
JSON object response format. An older method of generating JSON responses.
Using `json_schema` is recommended for models that support it. Note that the
model will not generate JSON without a system or user message instructing it
to do so.

type.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_object`.

oneOf.title: JSON object

anyOf.description:
Constrains the verbosity of the model's response. Lower values will result in
more concise responses, while higher values will result in more verbose responses.
Currently supported values are `low`, `medium`, and `high`. The default is
`medium`.

tool_choice.description:
How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating
a response. See the `tools` parameter to see how to specify which tools
the model can call.

oneOf.description:
Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.

`none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message.

`auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or
more tools.

`required` means the model must call one or more tools.
oneOf.title: Tool choice mode

oneOf.description: Constrains the tools available to the model to a pre-defined set.

mode.description:
Constrains the tools available to the model to a pre-defined set.

`auto` allows the model to pick from among the allowed tools and generate a
message.

`required` requires the model to call one or more of the allowed tools.

tools.description:
A list of tool definitions that the model should be allowed to call.

For the Responses API, the list of tool definitions might look like:
```json
[
  { "type": "function", "name": "get_weather" },
  { "type": "mcp", "server_label": "deepwiki" },
  { "type": "image_generation" }
]
```

items.description: A tool definition that the model should be allowed to call.

type.description: Allowed tool configuration type. Always `allowed_tools`.

oneOf.title: Allowed tools

oneOf.description:
Indicates that the model should use a built-in tool to generate a response.
[Learn more about built-in tools](/docs/guides/tools).

type.description:
The type of hosted tool the model should to use. Learn more about
[built-in tools](/docs/guides/tools).

Allowed values are:
- `file_search`
- `web_search_preview`
- `computer`
- `computer_use_preview`
- `computer_use`
- `code_interpreter`
- `image_generation`

oneOf.title: Hosted tool

oneOf.description: Use this option to force the model to call a specific function.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

type.description: For function calling, the type is always `function`.

oneOf.title: Function tool

oneOf.description: Use this option to force the model to call a specific tool on a remote MCP server.

anyOf.description: The name of the tool to call on the server.

server_label.description: The label of the MCP server to use.

type.description: For MCP tools, the type is always `mcp`.

oneOf.title: MCP tool

oneOf.description: Use this option to force the model to call a specific custom tool.

name.description: The name of the custom tool to call.

type.description: For custom tool calling, the type is always `custom`.

oneOf.title: Custom tool

type.description: The tool to call. Always `programmatic_tool_calling`.

oneOf.description: Forces the model to call the apply_patch tool when executing a tool call.

type.description: The tool to call. Always `apply_patch`.

oneOf.title: Specific apply patch tool choice

oneOf.description: Forces the model to call the shell tool when a tool call is required.

type.description: The tool to call. Always `shell`.

oneOf.title: Specific shell tool choice

tools.description:
An array of tools the model may call while generating a response. You
can specify which tool to use by setting the `tool_choice` parameter.

We support the following categories of tools:
- **Built-in tools**: Tools that are provided by OpenAI that extend the
  model's capabilities, like [web search](/docs/guides/tools-web-search)
  or [file search](/docs/guides/tools-file-search). Learn more about
  [built-in tools](/docs/guides/tools).
- **MCP Tools**: Integrations with third-party systems via custom MCP servers
  or predefined connectors such as Google Drive and SharePoint. Learn more about
  [MCP Tools](/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).
- **Function calls (custom tools)**: Functions that are defined by you,
  enabling the model to call your own code with strongly typed arguments
  and outputs. Learn more about
  [function calling](/docs/guides/function-calling). You can also use
  custom tools to call your own code.

items.description: A tool that can be used to generate a response.

oneOf.description: Defines a function in your own code the model can choose to call. Learn more about [function calling](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling).

anyOf.description: The tool invocation context(s).

defer_loading.description: Whether this function is deferred and loaded via tool search.

anyOf.description: A description of the function. Used by the model to determine whether or not to call the function.

op openai-response-get(response_id: String) -> Any
  description "Retrieve one stored model response by id"
  risk "low"
  idempotency "idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://api.openai.com"

operations.description: Create a chat completion through OpenRouter, routed to the named model. Billed per input and output token, so the caller must state a token budget via max_completion_tokens

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to route to, as `<author>/<slug>` — e.g. `openai/gpt-4o` or `anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`

parameters.name: messages
parameters.description: The conversation so far: a list of `{role, content}` objects, where role is one of system, developer, user, assistant or tool

parameters.name: max_completion_tokens
parameters.description: Upper bound on generated tokens, including reasoning tokens. Required by this connector so that every call states its cost bound

choices.description: One entry per completion; this connector never sets `n`, so there is exactly one

error.description: Present when the upstream provider failed *after* routing succeeded: `{code, message, metadata}`, delivered with HTTP 200 and no content. Check for it before reading `message`

finish_reason.description: The normalized reason generation stopped — `stop`, `length`, `tool_calls`, `content_filter`. Branch on this one

message.description: The assistant's turn: `role`, `content`, and `tool_calls` when the model called a tool

native_finish_reason.description: The upstream provider's own unmapped reason, whose vocabulary varies by provider

id.description: The generation's id, which is also what `GET /api/v1/generation` would be queried by — an operation this connector cannot express (C-30)

model.description: The model that actually served the request. It can differ from the one asked for when routing falls back

provider.description: The upstream provider that served it, e.g. `Anthropic` or `Together`. OpenRouter's own addition to the OpenAI shape and not part of the documented response schema, so it is recorded as optional

usage.description: `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`, and OpenRouter's own `cost` — what the call charged in credits, the same unit `openrouter-credits-get` reports

operations.flux:
op openrouter-chat-completion(model: String, messages: List<Any>, max_completion_tokens: Number) -> Any
  description "Create a chat completion through OpenRouter, routed to the named model. Billed per input and output token, so the caller must state a token budget via max_completion_tokens"
  risk "medium"
  idempotency "non_idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://openrouter.ai"
  url = fmt("{base}/api/v1/chat/completions")
  content_type = "application/json"
  payload = { max_completion_tokens, messages, model }
  response = http.request(body: payload, headers: { "content-type": content_type }, method: "POST", url)
  return response

credentials.name: pagerduty.api_token
credentials.description: PagerDuty REST API access key, sent as the Authorization header after the literal `Token token=`. A read-only key satisfies the four read operations; the two incident writes need a full-access key

operations.description: List the incidents this key can see, across every service it has access to. Returns one page; read `more` to learn whether another page exists, and page by adding `limit` to `offset`. No status, service, team or time filter is offered by this connector — see pagerduty-incident-get to inspect one incident in full

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of incidents to return in this page. PagerDuty caps this at 100

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of incidents to skip before this page begins. To read the next page, add the `limit` just used to the `offset` just used — this is not a page number

acknowledgements.description: Who has acknowledged the incident and when, each `{at, acknowledger}`. Empty unless status is acknowledged

alert_counts.description: How many alerts rolled up into this incident, `{all, triggered, resolved}`

assignments.description: Who the incident is currently assigned to, each `{at, assignee}` where `assignee` is a user reference

escalation_policy.description: A reference to the escalation policy governing this incident

html_url.description: The PagerDuty web UI URL a human would open

id.description: The incident's own id — pass this as `id` to pagerduty-incident-get, -acknowledge or -resolve

incident_key.description: The deduplication key the triggering integration supplied, when it supplied one

incident_number.description: The account-scoped sequence number PagerDuty displays, distinct from `id`

priority.description: A reference to the account's configured priority level, when the account uses priorities; null otherwise

resolved_at.description: Null until the incident is resolved

self.description: The API URL of this incident

service.description: A reference to the service this incident is on: `{id, type, summary, self, html_url}`. Pass its `id` to nothing here — pagerduty-service-list returns the full representation

status.description: triggered means nobody has taken it; acknowledged means somebody is working it and escalation has paused; resolved is terminal

summary.description: A short human-readable label for the incident, usually its title

teams.description: References to the teams the incident is visible to

urgency.description: Whether the service's escalation policy pages immediately (high) or notifies without paging (low)

limit.description: The limit this page was read with

more.description: True when another page exists past this one. This is the only continuation signal PagerDuty sends — there is no cursor

offset.description: The offset this page was read from

total.description: The total matching incidents. Null unless the request asked for it, which this connector does not

operations.flux:
op pagerduty-incident-list(limit: Number, offset: Number) -> Any
  description "List the incidents this key can see, across every service it has access to. Returns one page; read `more` to learn whether another page exists, and page by adding `limit` to `offset`. No status, service, team or time filter is offered by this connector — see pagerduty-incident-get to inspect one incident in full"
  risk "low"
  idempotency "idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://api.pagerduty.com"
  url = fmt("{base}/incidents")
  Accept = "application/vnd.pagerduty+json;version=2"
  response = http.request(headers: { Accept }, method: "GET", query: { limit, offset }, url)
  return response

operations.description: Acknowledge one incident, on behalf of a named PagerDuty user. This stops the escalation clock and tells the rotation that somebody is working the incident; it does not close it. PagerDuty refuses the change if the incident is already resolved, and answers that as data rather than as a failure

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The incident's own id, from pagerduty-incident-list's `id` field

parameters.name: from_email
parameters.description: The login address of the PagerDuty user this acknowledgement is recorded against. It must belong to a user in this PagerDuty account; PagerDuty answers 400 otherwise. A REST API key carries no user identity of its own, which is why this cannot be inferred

parameters.name: incident_type
parameters.description: Constant `incident_reference` — PagerDuty's discriminator for a partial incident object in a write. Not caller-supplied

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Constant `acknowledged` — not caller-supplied. Resolving is pagerduty-incident-resolve, a separate operation with its own risk classification

incident.description: The incident after the update, in the shape pagerduty-incident-get returns. Read `status` back to confirm the acknowledgement took effect

acknowledgements.description: Each `{at, acknowledger}`; the acknowledger is the user named by the From header

status.description: `acknowledged` after a successful call

operations.flux:
op pagerduty-incident-acknowledge(id: String, from_email: String) -> Any
  description "Acknowledge one incident, on behalf of a named PagerDuty user. This stops the escalation clock and tells the rotation that somebody is working the incident; it does not close it. PagerDuty refuses the change if the incident is already resolved, and answers that as data rather than as a failure"
  risk "medium"
  idempotency "idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://api.pagerduty.com"
  url = fmt("{base}/incidents/{id}")
  content_type = "application/json"
  Accept = "application/vnd.pagerduty+json;version=2"
  incident_type = "incident_reference"
  status = "acknowledged"
  payload = { incident: { status, type: incident_type } }
  response = http.request(body: payload, headers: { Accept, From: from_email, "content-type": content_type }, method: "PUT", url)
  return response

parameters.description: The HTML body. Postmark requires at least one of `text_body` or `html_body`; this schema cannot express that cross-field rule and does not enforce it

parameters.name: reply_to

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: A short label for categorizing this message in Postmark's activity view and statistics

MessageID.description: Postmark's id for this send; the handle for later bounce or delivery-stat lookups

operations.description: Post a message to a Slack channel, visible to everyone in it. Slack answers HTTP 200 even on failure: check `ok` in the response body before treating the message as sent

channel.description: The channel the message landed in, always as an id (`C0123ABCDEF`) even when the request named it

error.description: Present only when `ok` is false: Slack's machine-readable failure code, such as `channel_not_found`, `not_in_channel` or `msg_too_long`

message.description: The message as Slack stored it: `text`, `type`, `subtype`, `ts`, `bot_id`, `username`, and `attachments` when there are any

operations.description: Open a new incident on this status page. It is public the moment this call returns — anyone loading the page sees it, and with deliver_notifications true Statuspage emails and texts every subscriber the page has. The incident itself is reversible (resolve it, or delete it), but a notification that has been sent cannot be recalled, so treat deliver_notifications as the irreversible half of this call

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The incident's title, shown on the public status page and used as the subject line of the notification. Write it for the page's readers, not for an operator

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The lifecycle stage this incident opens in. investigating means the cause is not yet known; identified means it is; monitoring means a fix is deployed and being watched; resolved opens the incident already closed, which is how a retroactive record of a past outage is posted

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The first update's message, shown publicly under the incident and sent verbatim to subscribers if deliver_notifications is true. This is the text the outside world reads, so it must not contain internal hostnames, customer identifiers or anything else not meant to leave the organisation

parameters.name: deliver_notifications
parameters.description: Whether to notify subscribers. true emails and texts every subscriber this page has, immediately and irreversibly; false publishes the incident to the page silently. There is no default here on purpose — publishing to a public page is a choice about an audience, and this connector requires it to be made explicitly on every call

id.description: The new incident's id — what statuspage-incident-get and statuspage-incident-update address it by

impact.description: Statuspage's own calculation for the new incident

incident_updates.description: The one update this call posted

shortlink.description: The public short URL for this incident — already live

status.description: Echoes the status just set

operations.description: Capture an authorized payment intent, charging the customer the **full** authorized amount. Only a payment intent in `requires_capture` can be captured; a partial capture needs an `amount` this connector cannot send. Stripe answers 402 with an `error.code` such as `card_declined` when the capture is refused, and that arrives as data rather than as a failure
operations.repeatable_because: the connector requires an `Idempotency-Key` header on every call, and Stripe replays a keyed POST from its own cache for 24 hours rather than re-executing it, so a retried capture captures once and returns the first result

parameters.name: payment_intent
parameters.description: The id of the payment intent to capture, `pi_` followed by an opaque identifier. It must be in `requires_capture` — check with `stripe-payment-intent-get` first

parameters.name: idempotency_key
parameters.description: A unique string — a UUID is the convention — identifying this capture attempt. Stripe replays the first result for 24 hours rather than capturing again, so a retry with the same key is safe and a retry with a new key charges the customer twice. Generate it once per intent you mean to capture, and reuse it across retries

amount_received.description: What was actually taken. Equals `amount` after a full capture

status.description: `succeeded` after a successful capture

operations.description: List Stripe account events for operational visibility without replaying or changing an event

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.

items.description:
Snapshot events allow you to track and react to activity in your Stripe integration. When
the state of another API resource changes, Stripe creates an `Event` object that contains
all the relevant information associated with that action, including the affected API
resource. For example, a successful payment triggers a `charge.succeeded` event, which
contains the `Charge` in the event's data property. Some actions trigger multiple events.
For example, if you create a new subscription for a customer, it triggers both a
`customer.subscription.created` event and a `charge.succeeded` event.

Configure an event destination in your account to listen for events that represent actions
your integration needs to respond to. Additionally, you can retrieve an individual event or
a list of events from the API.

[Connect](https://docs.stripe.com/connect) platforms can also receive event notifications
that occur in their connected accounts. These events include an account attribute that
identifies the relevant connected account.

You can access events through the [Retrieve Event API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events#retrieve_event)
for 30 days.

account.description: The connected account that originates the event.

api_version.description: The Stripe API version used to render `data` when the event was created. The contents of `data` never change, so this value remains static regardless of the API version currently in use. This property is populated only for events created on or after October 31, 2014.

context.description: Authentication context needed to fetch the event or related object.

created.description: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

object.description: Object containing the API resource relevant to the event. For example, an `invoice.created` event will have a full [invoice object](https://api.stripe.com#invoice_object) as the value of the object key.

previous_attributes.description: Object containing the names of the updated attributes and their values prior to the event (only included in events of type `*.updated`). If an array attribute has any updated elements, this object contains the entire array. In Stripe API versions 2017-04-06 or earlier, an updated array attribute in this object includes only the updated array elements.

id.description: Unique identifier for the object.

livemode.description: If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.

object.description: String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.

pending_webhooks.description: Number of webhooks that haven't been successfully delivered (for example, to return a 20x response) to the URLs you specify.

id.description: ID of the API request that caused the event. If null, the event was automatic (e.g., Stripe's automatic subscription handling). Request logs are available in the [dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/logs), but currently not in the API.

idempotency_key.description: The idempotency key transmitted during the request, if any. *Note: This property is populated only for events on or after May 23, 2017*.

request.description: Information on the API request that triggers the event.

type.description: Description of the event (for example, `invoice.created` or `charge.refunded`).

items.title: NotificationEvent

has_more.description: True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.

object.description: String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.

url.description: The URL where this list can be accessed.

`ExchangeRate` objects allow you to determine the rates that Stripe is currently
using to convert from one currency to another. Since this number is variable

- *localize prices for processing payments on Stripe*
- *reconcile Stripe transactions*
- *determine how much money to send to a connected account*
- *determine app fees to charge a connected account*

*Using this Exchange Rates API beta for any purpose other than to transact on Stripe is strictly prohibited and constitutes a violation of Stripe's terms of service.*

operations.description: List one form's responses, newest first by default. Paginate with `before`/`after`, each naming the `token` of a response already retrieved, to page toward older or newer responses respectively; `page_size` alone returns only the first page. Each response's `answers` holds whatever that respondent typed or selected — this connector never inspects or filters on answer content

parameters.name: form_id
parameters.description: The form's own id, from typeform-form-list's `id` field, or the trailing path segment of the form's own URL (the part after `/to/`)

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Responses per page; Typeform defaults this to 25 and caps it at 1000

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return only responses submitted before this response's own `token` (exclusive) — the cursor for paging toward older responses. Pass the `token` field of the oldest response already retrieved. Omit on the first page

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return only responses submitted after this response's own `token` (exclusive) — the cursor for paging toward newer responses. Pass the `token` field of the newest response already retrieved. Omit on the first page

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only include responses at or after this UTC instant, written with no timezone suffix at all, e.g. "2017-07-09T00:00:00" — never a trailing "Z" or a "+HH:MM" offset. Which timestamp this filters (submitted_at, staged_at or landed_at) depends on which response_type is requested

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Only include responses at or before this UTC instant, written with no timezone suffix at all, e.g. "2017-07-09T00:00:00" — never a trailing "Z" or a "+HH:MM" offset. Which timestamp this filters (submitted_at, staged_at or landed_at) depends on which response_type is requested

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: Restrict to one or more submission states, comma-separated: started, partial, completed. Omit to receive every state

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: How to order the returned responses: a fixed field name and a direction, comma-separated

items.description: This page's responses, in the order `sort` (or the default) puts them

answers.description: One entry per answered question: at minimum `{field: {id, ref, type}, type}` plus exactly one value key named after `type` (text, choice, choices, email, number, boolean, date, url, file_url or payment). The value itself is whatever the respondent typed or selected and is never enumerated or exemplified here

calculated.description: Computed values Typeform's scoring feature attaches

hidden.description: Hidden-field values this response's session was launched with, keyed by the form's own hidden-field variable names (see typeform-form-get's `hidden`). Shape and content depend entirely on the form's own configuration — commonly an email address, a customer id or similar, so this connector never enumerates or exemplifies a value here

landing_id.description: Identifies the browsing session that landed on the form — distinct from the response itself

metadata.description: The submission's own browsing context — browser, platform, referer and network id. Not respondent-authored content

response_id.description: The same value as `token`, under Typeform's other name for it

submitted_at.description: Present once submitted; absent on a still-open partial response

token.description: This response's own opaque id: 32 lowercase hex characters. Pass it as `before` or `after` to page around it

operations.description: Get a collection's own schema: its display name, slug, and the full list of fields the site owner defined for it — each field's id, slug, display name, type, and whether it is required. This is the honest way to learn what an item's fieldData will contain, since that shape is tenant-defined and unknowable at compile time; this connector cannot type fieldData any more precisely than this lets a caller discover it

type.description: Webflow's field type, e.g. PlainText, RichText, Number, Bool, Date, Image, Link, Reference, MultiReference, Option, Color — not enumerated further as a closed set, since Webflow may add types this file does not yet know about

operations.description: Publish a site's currently staged changes to its live, public domains — every connected custom domain and the Webflow-hosted subdomain. This has immediate public effect: whatever is staged goes live for every visitor as soon as this call returns, with no separate confirmation step. Takes no body — Webflow's optional custom-domain selector is itself an array this connector cannot express (C-185), so this always publishes to every connected domain rather than a caller-chosen subset

parameters.name: site_id
parameters.description: The site's id, as returned by webflow-site-list

operations.flux:
op webflow-site-publish(site_id: String) -> Any
  description "Publish a site's currently staged changes to its live, public domains — every connected custom domain and the Webflow-hosted subdomain. This has immediate public effect: whatever is staged goes live for every visitor as soon as this call returns, with no separate confirmation step. Takes no body — Webflow's optional custom-domain selector is itself an array this connector cannot express (C-185), so this always publishes to every connected domain rather than a caller-chosen subset"
  risk "high"
  idempotency "non_idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://api.webflow.com/v2"
  url = fmt("{base}/sites/{site_id}/publish")
  response = http.request(method: "POST", url)
  return response

clientAssociations.description:
Represents the clients that are active in the conversation for a particular
user. A participant can have multiple clientAssociations in the case of
channel transfer, business initiated conversations, or identified users.
The order of the array indicates how recently a client has interacted with
the conversation, with the most recent client first. The first item in the
array is considered to be the user's primary client for that conversation,
and will be selected first for message delivery.

userId.description: The id of the associated user.

operations.flux:
op zendesk-messaging-message-create(conversationId: String, author: Any, content: Any) -> Any
  description "Post Message"
  risk "high"
  idempotency "non_idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/sc"
  appId = "{appId}"
  url = fmt("{base}/v2/apps/{appId}/conversations/{conversationId}/messages")
  content_type = "application/json"
  payload = { author, content }
  response = http.request(body: payload, headers: { "content-type": content_type }, method: "POST", url)
  return response

operations.flux:
op zendesk-messaging-message-list(conversationId: String) -> Any
  description "List Messages"
  risk "low"
  idempotency "idempotent"
  effects ["network"]
  expose true

  base = "https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/sc"
  appId = "{appId}"
  url = fmt("{base}/v2/apps/{appId}/conversations/{conversationId}/messages")
  response = http.request(method: "GET", url)
  return response
